title: Bedroom or study major opening offset 1.5 m from a parallel adjoining opening
text: Notwithstanding C3.10.2, a major opening to a bedroom or study may be offset a minimum of 1.5m from a parallel major opening on an adjoining property, measured from the edge of one major opening to another (refer Figure 3.10g).

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 2 - Single Houses.pdf

notes: Alternative to C3.10.2 screening for bedroom and study openings only; measured edge to edge between the two parallel openings (proposed fact). Note on p45: offsetting gives an oblique view but may not address overlooking of other floor levels or active habitable spaces of the adjoining property. Table 3.10a applies to sources with a floor level more than 0.5 m above NGL. The cone of vision radius includes the width of any adjoining ROW, communal street or battleaxe leg (p45 note). Applies to development adjoining an existing dwelling; vacant or unknown adjoining sites are C3.10.4. Coding excludes R100-SL: Table 2.10a removes all 3.10 provisions for R100-SL, but its footnote restores them where the development abuts a property not coded R100-SL (not encoded).
